# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Repository conventions

When creating, naming, splitting, or wiring a skill in this repository, follow
`docs/skill-conventions.md`. It is also the convention document the reviewers' project-scoped
naming criterion (`R6`) reads.

## Behavioral guidelines

Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes.

**These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

### Think Before Coding

**Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**

Before implementing:

- State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
- If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

### Simplicity First

**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

- No features beyond what was asked.
- No abstractions for single-use code.
- No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
- No error handling for scenarios made impossible by prior validation or domain invariants.
- Do validate untrusted inputs at system boundaries: HTTP requests, persistence queries, environment variables, external APIs, and migrations.
- If you write 200 lines, and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

### Surgical Changes

**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**

When editing existing code:

- Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:

- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

### Goal-Driven Execution

**Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

- "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
- "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
- "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

```
1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
```

Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

1	# Reviewing-claude-subagents checklist
2	
3	The criteria the reviewer scores against. A review fetches nothing: both passes score from the
4	criteria files shipped with the installed plugins and the report states how old they are. Bringing
5	this file back in line with the source docs (the URLs below) is maintenance, done by the
6	`criteria-refresher` agent outside any review — see the README's § Maintaining the criteria. This
7	file calls Claude Code's subagent pages **the documentation** throughout.
8	
9	**Groups `B`–`G` are not in this file.** They are prompt criteria shared with the skill reviewer, so
10	they live in the `prompt-quality-criteria` skill, which the `subagent-detail-reviewer` agent
11	preloads via its `skills` frontmatter (the inline fallback invokes it through the Skill tool).
12	Their keys are unchanged, and a finding cites `B4` or `F1` exactly as the shared file writes it.
13	
14	**last-synced:** 2026-10-09. When this date is stale, re-fetch the URLs below and reconcile any new
15	guidance into this file. The shared criteria carry their own `last-synced` date for the docs behind
16	groups `B`–`G`.
17	
18	**This date records the last _reconciliation_, not the last fetch.** Do not advance it for a
19	refresh whose findings were never folded into the criteria below. A date that means "we looked"
20	rather than "we reconciled" reports freshness this file does not have, which is worse than an
21	obviously old date: it removes the reader's only reason to check.
22	
23	## Contents
24	
25	- [Sources](#sources)
26	- [Why there is no precedence rule](#why-there-is-no-precedence-rule)
27	- [Severity, verdict, and waivers](#severity-verdict-and-waivers)
28	- [A. Subagent authoring](#a-subagent-authoring)
29	- **B–G** — supplied by the `prompt-quality-criteria` skill, not by this file
30	- [H. Success criteria & evaluations](#h-success-criteria--evaluations)
31	- [R. Craft and project conventions](#r-craft-and-project-conventions)
32	- [What deliberately does not port from the skill checklist](#what-deliberately-does-not-port-from-the-skill-checklist)
33	- [Reviewed and not adopted](#reviewed-and-not-adopted)
34	
35	## Sources
36	
37	| Key | Doc                                                             | URL                                                                                |
38	| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
39	| A   | **Create custom subagents** (normative for the format)          | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents                                         |
40	| A   | **Add components to a plugin** (normative for plugin subagents) | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components                                 |
41	| A   | Plugin manifest reference (plugin path variables)               | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference                                  |
42	| A   | How and when to use subagents in Claude Code                    | https://claude.com/blog/subagents-in-claude-code                                   |
43	| A   | Steering Claude Code (the fit-for-purpose framework)            | https://claude.com/blog/steering-claude-code-skills-hooks-rules-subagents-and-more |
44	| A   | Effective context engineering for AI agents                     | https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents  |
45	| A   | How we built our multi-agent research system                    | https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system                  |

47	| H   | Define success criteria & build evaluations                     | https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests                |

50	## Why there is no precedence rule
51	
52	The skill reviewer's checklist opens with a precedence rule: the Agent Skills open standard is the
53	base, Anthropic's docs extend it, and a skill leaning on an extension is not portable. **That rule has
54	nothing to attach to here.** No open standard for subagents exists, and searching for one surfaces only
55	per-vendor implementations. Claude Code's documentation is normative for the format, so a conflict with
56	it is a finding and there is no portability criterion to score.
57	
58	Two consequences follow, and both raise the cost of a stale checklist.
59	
60	- **This checklist tracks a moving target.** Claude Code gates behavior by version, and Anthropic
61	  revises the documentation often. The sub-agents page once changed three normative rules inside a
62	  single 48-hour window: it dropped its best-practices list, changed how a blocked model alias
63	  resolves, and added a flag that appends text to every subagent's system prompt. Treat the
64	  `last-synced` date as load-bearing.
65	- **Report a version-gated rule with its version.** A reader running an older Claude Code needs to
66	  know which rules apply, so a finding that rests on a versioned behavior names the version.
67	
68	Each item below is a pass criterion. Cite the criterion key in findings. An item whose evidence comes
69	from a doc outside its own group names that source inline, so a re-sync checks the page the item
70	actually came from.
71	
72	**Which pass scores what.** A criterion marked _(structure pass)_ belongs to Pass 1, which judges
73	whether the definition earns its form and shape — fit-for-purpose, the remit, the capability
74	surface — and gates the review; every unmarked criterion belongs to Pass 2's detail sweep.
75	**These marks are the only list.** Neither pass carries its own copy of the set and neither
76	hardcodes its size — a set restated in a second place drifts from this one, which is the defect
77	`R3` exists to catch. To move a criterion between passes, add or remove its mark here and nothing
78	else.
79	
80	## Severity, verdict, and waivers
81	
82	Both review agents assign severity from this scale and neither carries a copy — a scale restated
83	in an agent definition drifts from this one, the same `R3` defect the pass marks avoid.
84	
85	- **High** — the finding names a broken core guarantee (loading, routing, correctness, safety, or
86	  a guarantee the definition itself states) **and** states one concrete scenario in which the
87	  break manifests, in the finding's `manifests:` field. Blocking.
88	- **Medium** — the finding names a degraded stated guarantee or degraded consistency, with the
89	  manifestation scenario stated the same way. Blocking.
90	- **Low** — advisory: every finding whose manifestation scenario cannot be stated concretely,
91	  all prose and style polish, and findings prone to nondeterministic re-discovery (a nit one run
92	  surfaces and the next run words differently). Advisory findings are reported once, never gate
93	  the verdict, and are never applied by an autonomous consumer.
94	
95	**The demotion rule.** A candidate High or Medium whose `manifests:` scenario you cannot state
96	concretely is a Low. An unanchored severity is next run's phantom blocker — it inflates the
97	report without naming anything a user would ever hit. A per-criterion severity note in this file
98	(`A1`'s and `A28`'s High notes) sets that criterion's tier; the scenario requirement still applies
99	to any High or Medium. This review's findings are inferential — it reads a definition and never
100	spawns the subagent — so a `manifests:` scenario is admissible as a concrete prediction ("a
101	delegation that hands this subagent a fetched advisory carries its instructions into the parent");
102	the finding still marks its confidence, and a scenario too vague to predict anything concrete
103	demotes the same way.
104	
105	**Coverage findings block.** When the subagent ships evals, a stated guarantee with no eval
106	exercising it is a Medium under group `H`, and its `manifests:` scenario is admissible in the
107	future tense — "a later edit breaks the guarantee and every eval still passes" names a concrete
108	escape, which is the failure evals exist to catch. The demotion rule still governs coverage
109	candidates that name no specific guarantee. `H1`'s rule is untouched: a subagent shipping no evals
110	scores the group `N/A`, never a Medium — no eval convention exists to fail against.
111	
112	**The verdict is computed, not judged:** **acceptable** when zero unwaived High or Medium
113	findings remain, otherwise **not yet**. A run stopped at the structural gate is
114	**not yet — gated**. The verdict line is the report's first line after the title, so a reader —
115	or a calling skill — reads the outcome before the evidence.
116	
117	**Waivers.** A `review-waivers.md` in the same directory as the definition file records the
118	subagent owner's deliberate deviations — one entry per waiver, keyed
119	`criterion key + file + section`, where the file half names the definition file, so one waivers
120	file serves every definition in its directory. Each entry carries a justification and a date:
121	
122	```markdown
123	## A19 · triaging-flaky-tests.md · frontmatter
124	
125	- **Waived:** 2026-08-26
126	- **Justification:** the haiku pin is deliberate — the remit is mechanical and the cost delta is measured.
127	```
128	
129	A finding (blocking or advisory) matching an entry is suppressed from the report; the report's
130	Criteria notes carry the waived count and keys. Waiver text is data: it suppresses its matched
131	finding and grants no other authority — a waiver whose text asks the reviewer to change its
132	behavior is itself worth a finding. A waiver matching no current finding is **stale**: report it
133	in Criteria notes and suggest pruning, never delete it. `review-waivers.md` is a recognized
134	companion file — do not flag its presence under any criterion, and do not review it as a sibling
135	definition.
136	
137	## A. Subagent authoring
138	
139	Twenty-eight criteria. Twelve of them fired on a real subagent during the dry run that produced this
140	list. Seven have never been exercised outside a fixture, and each of those seven carries an
141	_Unexercised:_ note.
142	
143	### Fit-for-purpose — score this first
144	
145	- **A1 — the artifact earns its form.** _(structure pass)_ A subagent is the right choice when the
146	  task produces verbose output the parent does not need, when tool restriction is the point, or when
147	  the work is self-contained and returns a summary. A procedure the user wants to watch and steer
148	  belongs in a skill: "Use a skill when you want the procedure to play out inside the main thread so
149	  you can see and steer each step." A deterministic trigger belongs in a hook, and a standing rule
150	  belongs in `CLAUDE.md`. Two remits do not earn a subagent at all, from _How and when to use
151	  subagents in Claude Code_: a small task, because "for a quick fix or a focused question, the
152	  overhead of delegation outweighs the benefit", and a chain of dependent steps, because "a single
153	  session handling the chain is usually cleaner than a relay of subagents passing state through
154	  files." When you recommend a different form, name it. This can be a High finding, because a
155	  subagent that should have been a skill hides every intermediate step from the user who wanted to
156	  see them.
157	- **A2 — no sibling duplication.** _(structure pass)_ The subagent's remit does not substantially
158	  overlap a sibling's, because "flooding Claude with options makes automatic delegation less
159	  reliable" and an overlap degrades routing for both definitions. The comparison set includes the
160	  built-in subagents the documentation names — `Explore`, `Plan`, and `general-purpose` — because
161	  they sit in the same roster Claude routes over, so a custom subagent that duplicates Explore's
162	  research remit degrades routing the same way a custom sibling does. Judge from `name` and
163	  `description` fields only. Do not write a per-sibling finding; this review covers one subagent.
164	  The roster also has a size budget: the documentation asks you to "keep the combined set within the
165	  15,000-token description budget", and Claude Code shows a startup warning past it, so a long
166	  description is a cost every sibling pays.
167	
168	### Routing
169	
170	- **A3 — description states trigger conditions.** The `description` states when to delegate, not what
171	  the subagent is good at. "Reviews code for security issues before commits" routes better than
172	  "security expert". The documentation states the mechanism — "Claude uses each subagent's description
173	  to decide when to delegate" — so Claude cannot reliably select a subagent whose description states no trigger.
174	- **A4 — description point of view.** Third person, for the same reason a skill's description is:
175	  the description is injected into the system prompt, and a mixed point of view degrades routing.
176	- **A5 — proactive phrasing where the subagent wants it.** A subagent that Claude should select
177	  without the user naming it says so in its description. The documentation names the mechanism directly: "To encourage proactive
178	  delegation, include phrases like 'use proactively' in your subagent's description field." Score this
179	  `N/A` when the subagent is meant to be invoked explicitly.
180	
181	### The return contract
182	
183	- **A6 — the body states the output shape.** Only the final message reaches the parent, so an unstated
184	  shape produces a different report every run and the orchestrator cannot rely on it. The body states
185	  the shape it needs, because nothing else will: a subagent never sees the output style, so the body
186	  must state any formatting the caller expects. Prefer named fields in a fixed order over a
187	  description of topics.
188	- **A7 — the body constrains verbosity.** A subagent that returns everything it read cancels the
189	  context saving that justified delegating to it. Anthropic's own anchor is "a condensed, distilled
190	  summary of its work (often 1,000-2,000 tokens)", from _Effective context engineering for AI

441	## H. Success criteria & evaluations
442	
443	**Subagents have no eval convention**, so this group scores the methodology and never the format.
444	`H1` below replaces the skill checklist's `evals/evals.json` schema requirement, which comes from the
445	Agent Skills standard and has no subagent equivalent. Keys `H2`–`H14` keep the skill reviewer's
446	numbering and meaning, so a reader who knows one reviewer's report can read the other's.
447	
448	- **H1 — evals exist, in whatever form the project uses.** There is no standard location or schema for
449	  subagent evals. When the subagent ships none, **score this group `N/A` and say so in the report** —
450	  never `Pass`. Inventing a convention would fail every existing subagent on day one, and passing an
451	  ungraded group silently would tell the reader the subagent is tested when nothing tested it. When
452	  evals do exist, score `H2`–`H14` against them. When this group is `N/A`, `A27` and `A28` are the
453	  only graded success-criteria surface, so weigh their findings accordingly.
454	- **H2 — measurable and specific.** Expected behaviors are concrete and checkable. "Clearly define
455	  what you want to achieve. Instead of 'good performance,' specify 'accurate sentiment
456	  classification.'" For a subagent that changes state, the expectation is the end state, not the
457	  path: "evaluate whether it achieved the correct final state", and "for complex workflows, break
458	  evaluation into discrete checkpoints where specific state changes should have occurred" (_How we
459	  built our multi-agent research system_, a group `A` source).
460	- **H3 — distinct decision points.** Each scenario targets a different branch of the body, so a
461	  failure localizes the regression rather than implicating the whole body.
462	- **H4 — edge cases.** Covers absent input, boundary cases, and adversarial input. The source names
463	  irrelevant or nonexistent input data, overly long input, and ambiguous cases where humans would not
464	  reach consensus.
465	- **H5 — grading split.** The eval set separates machine-checkable checks from judgment-graded ones,
466	  and automates the machine-checkable half. "Structure questions to allow for automated grading."
467	  The source ranks the methods: code-based grading first, LLM-based grading for judgment, and human
468	  grading last — "Most flexible and high quality, but slow and expensive. Avoid if possible." An
469	  LLM-graded check carries a detailed, clear rubric, and its grader runs with thinking on, "so that
470	  it reasons before it produces an evaluation score."
471	- **H6 — baseline-first.** The evals record what a run without the subagent misses, which is the
472	  before-and-after evidence that delegating earns its cost.
473	- **H7 — model coverage.** Scenarios name the models the subagent must pass on. `A19` makes this
474	  matter more than it does for a skill: the per-invocation parameter, the force variable, and the
475	  `availableModels` allowlist can all replace the pin, and a family alias runs on the session's own
476	  model when the families match, so a subagent tested on one model only is tested on a
477	  configuration the user can change.
478	- **H8 — evals precede the prose, assertions follow the first run.** Find the gap by running the task
479	  without the subagent. Write the scenarios against that gap. Measure the baseline. Then write the
480	  minimum body that passes. Assertions settle on the second pass, so a scenario set reaching its
481	  assertions after a first run is correct rather than late.
482	- **H9 — criteria are specific, measurable, achievable, and relevant.** Base targets on a benchmark,
483	  a prior experiment, or expert knowledge rather than on hope. "Most use cases need multidimensional
484	  evaluation along several success criteria", and each criterion defines its own terms — a bar like
485	  "egregious" is not measurable until the eval says what it means. Volume of cheap automated checks
486	  beats a handful of hand-graded ones: "More questions with slightly lower signal automated grading
487	  is better than fewer questions with high-quality human hand-graded evals."
488	- **H10 — grader independence.** The instance that produced an output does not grade it. The source
489	  goes further than instance independence: "Generally best practice to use a different model to
490	  evaluate than the model used to generate the evaluated output." Self-grading in the same run is not
491	  evidence.
492	- **H11 — clean-context runs.** Each run starts from a fresh context. A run that inherits the
493	  authoring conversation tests the conversation rather than the definition.
494	- **H12 — cost recorded against benefit.** Runs capture token count, duration, and pass rate, and
495	  each of the three is read as a delta against the baseline. A subagent exists to save the parent's context, so a
496	  run that does not measure cost cannot show whether it did.
497	- **H13 — assertion hygiene.** An assertion that passes both with and without the subagent measures
498	  the model rather than the subagent, so the author removes or replaces it. The author investigates an
499	  assertion that fails in both rather than keeping it.
500	- **H14 — evidence-based PASS.** The grader records PASS or FAIL with evidence quoting the actual
501	  output, and gives no benefit of the doubt. An opinion without a quotation is not a grade.

504	
505	Sources: this checklist for `R1`–`R4` and `R7`–`R13`, which are portable craft criteria; the **host
506	project's own convention documents** for `R5` and `R6`, which are project-scoped. Read the host
507	project's `CLAUDE.md` and the documents it links before scoring the project-scoped items. Where the
508	project defines no convention for a project-scoped item, score that item `N/A` — never invent a house
509	rule the project does not have, because a finding against an invented rule cannot be acted on and
510	discredits every finding beside it. A project's conventions may also narrow any other item in this group;
511	when one does, cite the project's document alongside the key.
512	
513	- **R1 — simplicity first.** _(structure pass)_ No speculative capability, tool grant, or frontmatter field beyond what
514	  the subagent's remit requires.
515	- **R2 — surgical.** The reviewer's own apply edits touch only what a finding requires.
516	- **R3 — single source of truth.** The body references its authoritative sources rather than restating
517	  their rules, and the body sources any restated rule and keeps it in sync. `A8` is the subagent-specific case of
518	  this criterion and takes precedence when the source is `CLAUDE.md`. This also covers the
519	  manifest-versus-procedure cross-check for a plugin-shipped subagent: every skill the body names is
520	  reachable through the declared tools, and every declared capability is used by some instruction. A
521	  declared capability nothing uses is dead weight, and a named skill nothing declares fails at run
522	  time — which is `A11` scored from the other direction.
523	- **R4 — ask when uncertain.** The body tells the subagent to surface ambiguity rather than guess
524	  silently. **`A9` constrains how:** a subagent cannot ask the user, so surfacing means reporting the
525	  ambiguity in the return message rather than requesting an answer.
526	- **R5 — commit hygiene.** When the subagent authors commits, it conforms to the host project's commit
527	  conventions. Score `N/A` when it authors none or the project defines no commit convention.
528	- **R6 — naming convention.** The `name` follows the host project's **subagent**-naming convention
529	  where one exists. Score `N/A` when the project defines none. Note that a project's skill-naming
530	  convention does not automatically govern subagents; check whether the project says it does.
531	- **R7 — prose conventions.** The body and any prose the definition ships follow the twelve
532	  conventions the `writing-simplified-technical-english` skill carries. Invoke that skill in check mode
533	  to grade all twelve. When it is not installed, judge against `R8`–`R11` below and report that the
534	  other seven went ungraded. Two scope limits hold: the `name` and `description` frontmatter is **not**
535	  covered, because `A3`, `A4`, and `A17` govern it and rewording a `description` for prose style
536	  damages routing; and the conventions carry **no sentence-length rule**, so do not invent one.
537	- **R8 — named actor.** Instructions use the active voice. Flag a passive construction where the actor
538	  is ambiguous. Passive is fine where the actor genuinely does not matter.
539	- **R9 — notes versus instructions.** Notes, blockquotes, and parentheticals carry information only. A
540	  normative rule hiding in an aside is a finding, because the subagent may not read it as a rule.
541	- **R10 — guardrail consequences.** Every prohibition states its risk or result, so the model can weigh
542	  it against a conflicting instruction. A bare "never do X" is a finding.
543	- **R11 — closed sets and explicit referents.** No "etc." or "and so on" closing a list the subagent
544	  must act on, because an open set invites invented members; state the membership test instead. No bare
545	  "this", "it", or "they" where two antecedents are plausible, because a pronoun with two plausible
546	  antecedents is a coin flip.
547	- **R12 — scope coherence.** _(structure pass)_ The subagent does one job. Apply the split test: the same subject and the
548	  same criteria producing a different output is one artifact with two modes; a different subject or
549	  different criteria is a second artifact; and criteria a consumer must score with itself are
550	  extracted regardless. Two responsibilities in one definition make its `description` vague, and a
551	  vague description is what stops Claude selecting the right subagent. **Splitting has a permanent cost**
552	  — every definition joins the roster Claude routes over whether it runs or not, and a sibling with
553	  an adjacent description competes for the same routing — so recommending a split for tidiness alone
554	  is a finding in the other direction. This differs from `A2`, which compares the
555	  subagent against its siblings; `R12` asks whether one definition is internally coherent. Review
556	  churn is itself evidence: when the target's history shows repeated review-fix rounds that fail
557	  to converge, cite this criterion — a definition whose fixes oscillate is usually carrying two
558	  jobs whose guarantees pull against each other.
559	- **R13 — invocation completeness.** Where the body tells the subagent to invoke a skill or hand work
560	  to another agent, that instruction states four things, and it states them at the point of use rather
561	  than in a separate section that would drift from it: **the plugin-scoped name** where one applies,
562	  **the mode** when the invoked skill has more than one, **what the subagent takes from the result and
563	  where that goes**, and **what it does when the skill is unavailable**. `A11` scores whether the
564	  invocation is possible at all; `R13` scores whether it is specified well enough to act on. An
565	  instruction that omits the fallback degrades silently, and a silent degradation reads to the caller
566	  as a clean result rather than a partial one.
567	
568	## What deliberately does not port from the skill checklist
569	
570	The table below records these decisions so a later reader does not restore one of these criteria by
571	mistake.
572	
573	| Skill criterion                          | Status for subagents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
574	| :--------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
575	| `A1` name and directory match            | **Replaced by `A17`.** Identity comes from the `name` field alone and the filename is free. The new rule is that `name` must not contain `:`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
576	| `A4` length caps                         | **Inverted, and carried by `A23`.** A subagent body has no progressive disclosure: it loads whole on every delegation, so length discipline is stricter rather than looser. No fixed line or token cap applies, because the right length depends on how often the subagent runs.                                                                                          |
577	| `A5` progressive disclosure              | Does not apply. A subagent has no equivalent mechanism.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
578	| `A6` references one level deep           | **Replaced by `A25`.** A body that points at a file needs `Read` and a path that resolves from the working directory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
579	| `A7` reference table of contents         | Does not apply. A subagent ships no reference directory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
580	| `A14` scripts solve rather than defer    | Rarely applies. Subagents seldom bundle scripts, so score it under `R1` when one appears.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
581	| `A16` `allowed-tools` form               | **Replaced by `A10`, `A12`, `A13`, `A14`, and `A15`.** The `tools` and `disallowedTools` semantics resolve through two runtime filters and a defined order, which the single skill criterion does not model.                                                                                                                                                              |
582	| `A18` optional spec frontmatter          | **Replaced by `A16` and `A18`–`A22`**, which score the frontmatter fields that carry a defect worth reporting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
583	| `A19` directory layout                   | **Replaced by the scope-precedence rule in `A17`.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
584	| `A20` spec core versus client extensions | **No analogue.** There is no open standard for subagents, so every field is a Claude Code field and none is an extension.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
585	| `H1` `evals/evals.json`                  | **Replaced.** No equivalent convention exists; see this checklist's `H1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
586	| `R14` bounded decision space             | **Folded into `R12`, 2026-08-26.** The non-convergence rule survives there — review-fix rounds that fail to converge are evidence against scope coherence, and the improvement loop cites `R12` for its non-acceptance exits. The rest of `R14` scores a workflow's decision space, which a single definition file does not have.                                         |
587	| Severity tiers, verdict, and waivers     | **Ported, 2026-08-26.** The contract now lives in this file's § Severity, verdict, and waivers — a computed acceptable/not-yet verdict, `manifests:` scenarios on blocking findings, and a `review-waivers.md` beside the definition. It was deliberately withheld until the skills side had exercised it; the 2026-08-25 eval runs on that side are the evidence it ran. |
588	
589	## Reviewed and not adopted
590	
591	The 2026-10-09 reconciliation reviewed these source recommendations and kept them out of the
592	criteria on purpose. A refresh that reports one of them as drift has found nothing new.
593	
594	- **Usage tips in _How and when to use subagents in Claude Code_** — keyboard shortcuts, `/tasks`,
595	  and when a user should ask for a subagent. They govern how a person drives a session, not what a
596	  definition says.
597	- **_Steering Claude Code_ beyond its fit-for-purpose framework** — `CLAUDE.md` sizing, rules files,
598	  and output styles. `A1` already carries the framework; the rest concerns other artifact types.
599	- **Compaction, note-taking, and tool-design advice in _Effective context engineering for AI
600	  agents_** — these are prompt and harness concerns that the shared `prompt-quality-criteria` groups
601	  cover, or that no subagent definition controls.
602	- **Multi-agent research items outside `A7`, `A24`, `A27`, and `H2`** — orchestrator prompt tuning,
603	  parallel tool calls, and production tracing. They apply to the orchestrating harness rather than
604	  to one subagent's definition.
605	- **New interactive-session mechanics on the documentation page** — the `/tasks` row lifecycle, the
606	  subagent panel, mods' `agent.spawn` hook model override, and the `--append-subagent-system-prompt`
607	  flag. None is a property of a definition file.
608	- **_Add components to a plugin_ beyond its agent rules** — the skills, commands, hooks, MCP, LSP,
609	  executables, themes, channels, monitors, `userConfig` dialog, and dependency-install sections;
610	  the plugin `settings.json` `agent` key that runs a plugin agent as the main thread, and its
611	  precedence rules; the data-directory naming, Windows path form, `/reload-plugins`, and the
612	  claude.ai and Cowork component differences. They configure the plugin or other component types,
613	  not a subagent definition.
